meta.title: Operation of Particle Size Analyzer in Central Instrumentation Laboratory

sections.purpose: To determine the particle size distribution of drug powders, nanoparticles, and pharmaceutical excipients using dynamic light scattering (DLS) or laser diffraction technology for formulation development and quality control.
sections.scope: Applicable to Central Instrumentation Laboratory for particle size characterization of drug suspensions, colloidal systems, nanoparticulate drug delivery systems, and bulk pharmaceutical powders.
procedure: Switch on the particle size analyzer and the associated PC; open the instrument software.
Allow 20–30 minutes warm-up for laser stabilization.

For DLS (nano-range, 1 nm–10 µm): prepare the sample in the appropriate dispersant (purified water, buffer, or organic solvent); ensure the sample is at a suitable concentration (optically translucent, not turbid).
Filter the dispersant through a 0.2 µm membrane filter to remove dust particles before use.
Set the refractive index and absorption parameters for the sample material in the software.
Clean the DLS cuvette with filtered dispersant (3 rinses); fill with sample.
Place the cuvette in the sample holder; ensure it is positioned correctly.
Set temperature to 25°C; equilibrate for 2 minutes.
Start the measurement; the software will run multiple acquisition cycles (typically 3–5 runs of 10–30 seconds each).
Record the Z-average diameter (mean hydrodynamic diameter), PDI (polydispersity index), and zeta potential if measured.
For laser diffraction (macro-range, 0.1–3500 µm): add the sample to the dispersant in the sample cell; set the appropriate optical model (Fraunhofer or Mie theory); start the measurement.
Record D10, D50, D90 values and the full size distribution graph.
Clean the cuvette or sample cell with 3–4 rinses of filtered dispersant immediately after use.
Record sample name, dispersant, temperature, results, and instrument parameters in the register.
precautions: Dust contamination is the most common source of error — always filter dispersants and prepare samples in a clean environment.
Use only scratch-free cuvettes — scratches cause laser scattering artefacts.
For DLS: sample concentration must be in the correct range — too concentrated causes multiple scattering; too dilute gives poor signal.
Allow temperature equilibration before each measurement — temperature affects Brownian motion and thus the calculated size.
Select the appropriate optical model (Fraunhofer vs. Mie) for the sample — incorrect model gives systematically wrong size distributions.
Clean the cuvette immediately after use — dried sample deposits are difficult to remove.
Calibrate the instrument with certified polystyrene size standards regularly.
